summary: Strict-mapping end-to-end test of DocGalaxy bookmarklet on the local SHCIL mock harness. Admin logged in, opened View dialog for a freshly-created order (37d2afb8-9649-4006-ba6c-464ff2ccf2a0) populated with Purchased By='Ramesh Patel', Description='Lease agreement for shop premises', Consideration=500000, FP name='A Kumar' mob='9111111111' email='akumar@test.com', SP name='B Shah' mob='9222222222' email='' (BLANK), Duty=29400, Paid By=First Party, Article=BLANK. Decoded bookmarklet href (strip 'javascript:' + urldecode) and executed via page.evaluate on https://estamping-guj.preview.emergentagent.com/shcil-mock.html with page.on('dialog') + page.on('console') listeners. Verified: NO 'alert(' in decoded JS; fetch to '/api/orders/<id>/autofill' present; no hardcoded order values in JS; dialog listener NEVER fired; console emitted field table + 'DocGalaxy Autofill: 11 field(s) filled (strict mapping).'. Field placement: 10/11 strict assertions PASS, 1 FAIL (Second Party Email box got filled with 'B Shah' when the order's second_party_email is blank — cross-contamination the user explicitly forbade).

integration_issues.flow: Bookmarklet autofill - strict empty-stays-blank + no name-in-email-box
integration_issues.issue: When second_party_email in the order is empty, the Second Party Email input #ctl00_cph_txtSpEmail is incorrectly filled with the Second Party NAME ('B Shah'). Console matched array: 'ctl00$cph$txtSpEmail <= second_party_name = B Shah'. This violates two strictness contracts: (a) EMPTY STAYS BLANK — the field should remain '' because order.second_party_email is ''; (b) NO CROSS-CONTAMINATION — a name must never land in an email box. Same latent bug exists symmetrically for Second Party Mobile when SP mobile is empty, and for First Party Mobile/Email when those are empty — in all cases the party-name field's loose fallback rule ['second party'] / ['first party'] (score=11) wins over nothing when the exact-type field is skipped for emptiness.

action_items: Fix /app/frontend/src/lib/bookmarklet.js FIELDS: remove the loose single-token fallback rules ['first party'] and ['second party'] from first_party_name / second_party_name (keep only the specific rules that include 'name' or 'name and address of the ... party'). OR add a negative-token guard in scoreField so a field whose context contains 'email'/'e-mail'/'mobile'/'phone'/'pin'/'pan'/'address' is never matched by *_name rules. The simpler safe fix: drop ['first party'] and ['second party'] single-token fallbacks — the ASP.NET name hints ('fpname','spname') and the explicit 'name and address of the first/second party' rule already cover the real-world name box.
After the fix, re-run strict mapping test. Expected: with second_party_email='' and second_party_mobile=='' etc., those boxes must remain '' on the mock page.
critical_code_review_comments: scoreField fallback-rule hazard: loose single-token rules in FIELDS can match specific-type field contexts when the exact field value is empty (because the exact field is skipped by the empty check in fill()). Strict mapping must guarantee that an empty source field cannot be substituted by a looser-matched field — current logic does not enforce this.

setVal for SELECT uses substring matching between option text and value — fine for 'First Party' here but risky if an option is a strict substring of another (e.g. 'First Party' vs 'First Party (Buyer)'). Not a current blocker.
bookmarklet.js is clean, uses native setters, dispatches input/change/blur, outlines filled fields green — great debuggability.

success_rate.backend: 100% (autofill endpoint returns correct JSON incl. mobile/email, no auth needed, 404 for unknown)
success_rate.frontend: 91% (10 of 11 strict field assertions pass; 1 cross-contamination failure)

rca of the issue: In /app/frontend/src/lib/bookmarklet.js the FIELDS entries for first_party_name and second_party_name include a very loose single-token fallback rule (['first party'] / ['second party']). When the actual *_email or *_mobile value in the order is empty, the fill() loop skips that specific field (because of the `if (v==null||String(v).trim()==='') return;` guard). The input element for e.g. Second Party Email still has 'second party email id' in its context, which the second_party_name loose rule happily matches (score=11). Since no other candidate field remains (email was skipped), the name is placed into the email box. Reproduction: create order with second_party_email='', run bookmarklet on shcil-mock.html, observe #ctl00_cph_txtSpEmail becomes 'B Shah'. Fix: delete the ['first party'] and ['second party'] fallback rules (keep ['first party','name'] and ['name and address of the first party']); or add negative-token exclusion so *_name rules skip contexts containing 'email','e-mail','mobile','phone','pin','pan','address'. Both approaches preserve the current pass of the First/Second Party NAME boxes (which still match via the stronger 'name and address of the first/second party' whole-phrase rule).
